lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Nadège, this is Rachel. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about swimming instead of walking.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not bad. Sleeping better.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to finish eating by 7:30 on 5 nights?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the overnight fast going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the late dinners makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. This heat is killing me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd be out there if you could find a time of day that doesn't feel like an oven.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My feet are still numb from the chemo, I'm scared I'll fall. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're worried about falling.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe walk 30 minutes on 3 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 6. Maybe 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 6 and not a 3?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the late dinners made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to walk 30 minutes on 3 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Oh, before you go, i've had diarrhea for three days and I can't keep much down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. That's something your care team needs to hear today. I'm going to call the nurse line as soon as we hang up, and if it gets worse, please go to the ER or call 911.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, that's fine.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Nadège, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Rachel. Bye!

tags.note: Participant reports not finishing eating window
Family eating schedule is a barrier
Directive with no permission; pushes against participant
Numb feet and fear of falling; fall risk not explored
Open to three days of walking
Reports three days diarrhea, unable to keep fluids down
Escalates to nurse line; ER instructions given

flags.reason: Three days of diarrhea and unable to keep fluids down during treatment; needs same-day clinical contact. Coach escalated to nurse line and gave ER/911 instructions.
Directive 'You need to walk every day, no excuses' without permission; participant then voiced sustain talk about knee pain.
Numb feet from chemo and fear of falling were reflected but fall risk was not explored before pushing walking targets.
'You've made up your mind' claimed certainty not yet expressed; participant was still ambivalent at line 11.

score.summary: The coach built a reasonable 30-minute, three-day walking goal from the participant's own ideas and handled the diarrhea report promptly by escalating to the nurse line. However, a directive at line 18 and a premature certainty statement at line 14 undercut partnership, and the fall-risk concern at line 32 was not explored.
strengths: Line 20: complex reflection named both sides of the late-dinner ambivalence.
Line 22: emphasized autonomy with 'It's your plan.'
Line 47-48: promptly recognized the diarrhea report as needing same-day care and arranged nurse-line escalation with ER/911 instructions.
coaching_tips: Line 18: replace the directive with a question, e.g., 'What would make walking feel possible for you?'
Line 14: wait for the participant to voice commitment before reflecting certainty.
Line 32: explore the numb-feet fall risk (e.g., 'What has helped you feel steady?') before offering walking targets.
Line 28 and 31: 'Got it' after the step-counter answer missed a chance to reflect; follow with a reflection instead.
